title: Кофе со снотворным  (Coffee with Sleeping Drops)

segments.t: Back at Claude Monet, Louis delivers a cup of coffee spiked with sleeping drops to German's office, and Senya and Fedya sneak in as soon as the boss slumps over his desk.
Лезь давай к нему в карман.
Да я руку не могу достать.
Let's walk through each line of the office infiltration.
'German Mikhailovich, here is your coffee.' In everyday Russian, 'Mikhailovich' flows straight into 'coffee' without extra linking words.
'Just the way you like it.' Literally 'everything how you love', this is a classic phrase servers use when presenting a favorite order.
'Why are you standing there, go on.' Starting with the everyday word for 'let us' is how Russian speakers warmly invite someone to do something together.
'And why does it have to be me right away?' Adding the adverb 'right away' highlights Fedya's protest at being volunteered first.
'Let's play rock, paper, scissors for it.' Notice that Russian lists the three items in the order 'stone, scissors, paper'.
'We already flipped a coin.' Senya pairs 'already' with 'to coin' directly, since spoken Russian skips English filler words like 'the', 'a', and 'is'.
'Maybe we should play the cities game too?' In spoken Russian, the words stay in their normal statement order and Fedya's rising voice at the end turns the line into a question.
Лезь давай к нему в карман.
'Go on, reach into his pocket.' Starting with the everyday word for 'let us' is how Russian speakers warmly invite someone to do something together.
'It is very funny to you, is it?' In spoken Russian, the words stay in their normal statement order and Fedya's rising voice at the end turns the line into a question.
'You had better help me instead.' Fedya pairs 'help' with 'better' directly, since spoken Russian skips English filler words like 'the', 'a', and 'is'.
'Well, what are you doing in here?' Louis whispers an urgent question using the colloquial adverb for 'here'.
Да я руку не могу достать.
'I cannot get my hand back out.' Here Fedya anchors the thought on 'arm' and finishes on 'to take out, to get, to reach', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
'I am afraid that he will wake up right now.' In everyday Russian, 'am afraid' flows straight into 'right' without extra linking words.
'He will not wake up, he is sleeping soundly.' Russian says someone sleeps 'strongly' or 'firmly' where English says 'soundly'. Now let's hear the whole scene again from start to finish.
Лезь давай к нему в карман.
Да я руку не могу достать.
Notice how Russian orders the hand game as 'rock, scissors, paper', and uses the dative pronoun when saying 'it is funny to you'. Until next time!
